source: Watermelon (ដំណាំ ឪឡឹក) cultivation factsheet, undated; source publisher not stated on the visible pages but the structure and layout are consistent with MAFF/GDA vegetable-crop factsheet series (elibrary.maff.gov.kh). Uploaded PDF, no cover page present.
text:
Two main planting methods are described for watermelon: direct seeding and transplanting of seedlings raised in nursery containers.

For direct seeding, seed should first be soaked in water for about 2 hours, then treated by soaking in a solution of the fungicide Captan 50% WP for 25-30 minutes (or by mixing about 2.5-3 g of Captan with 1 kg of seed) before sowing. Before sowing, farmers dig planting holes spaced about 1 m apart in rows, apply a small amount of the insecticide Furadan 3G (about 10 g per hole) into the hole, then sow 2-3 treated seeds per hole, cover with soil, and water within one to two days after sowing.

For transplanting seedlings raised in nursery trays, after seed treatment with Captan solution the seed is sown into nursery bags or plug trays filled with a mix of about 5% rice husk ash, 3 parts compost/manure, 1 part sandy soil, and 1 part fine soil (or similar ratios), mixed thoroughly; 2-3 treated seeds are placed per cell/bag. Seedlings should not be kept in the nursery for more than about 4 days beyond normal transplanting age; transplanting is typically done when seedlings are young to avoid root disturbance. After sowing or transplanting, watering is done regularly, tapering off as fruit approaches maturity to concentrate sugars, following weather and soil-moisture conditions rather than a rigid fixed schedule.

Watermelon can be grown by direct sowing or by transplanting depending on the local farming system and available resources; the growth cycle from sowing to fruit set/harvest generally runs about 3 months, with roughly 1200 mm of rainfall or equivalent irrigation and around 50% relative humidity being favorable over the season.
